title: Day-Summary Publishing Delay
dataSources: Photos (`photo:capture`), places visited (`location:visit`), voice memos (`voicememo:note`), logged moments (`lifelog:moment`), timeline events (`timeline:event`).
app: Life-logging and memory telemetry — photo libraries (Google Photos, Immich), location history, voice memos, and daily-moment journals — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lifelog:moment summary_published_epoch=*
| bin _time span=1d
| stats max(_time) as last_capture, max(summary_published_epoch) as summary_published_epoch by _time
| eval publish_lag_hours=round((summary_published_epoch-last_capture)/3600,1)
| sort - _time
description: Tracks how long it takes to turn a day's raw notes and captures into a finished day summary.
value: Publishing delay matters because summarization is where raw logging becomes useful reflection.
implementation: Add summary publish timestamps to life-log moments and calculate daily lag from last capture to finished summary.
visualization: Line chart of day-summary publishing lag in hours.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how long it takes to turn a day of raw notes into a finished summary you can revisit.
